firstMessage.rawMarkdown:
The overview explains scoring with a short example where four levels out of five is about 66.7 percent. The scorer that actually ships in the `arc_agi` package is stricter than that, and the gap is big enough to change what you optimise for. Here is the computation as it is written in `arc_agi/scorecard.py`.

For a level you complete:

    score = min((baseline_actions / actions_taken) ** 2 * 100, 115)

A level you do not complete scores 0.

A game is not the plain mean of those level scores. Each level is weighted by its level number, and the result is then capped by the share of level weight you actually finished:

    weighted = sum(level_score[i] * i) / sum(i)
    cap      = sum(i over completed levels) / sum(i) * 100
    game     = min(weighted, cap)

The leaderboard number is the plain mean of the per game scores.

Take cd82, which has six levels with baselines [55, 8, 41, 21, 23, 23]. The weights are 1 through 6 and sum to 21.

| what you do | game score |
|---|---|
| match the baseline on all six levels | 100.00 |
| take twice the baseline actions on all six | 25.00 |
| clear the first four perfectly, then stop | 47.62 |

The last row is the one worth sitting with. Four of six levels sounds like 66.7 percent, but those four carry weights 1+2+3+4 = 10 out of 21, so the weighted mean and the cap both land on 10/21, which is 47.62.

Two things follow from that.

Depth is worth more than efficiency. A level you never reach costs you its weight twice, once inside the mean and once through the cap, and the later levels carry the heavy weights. Getting to level 5 moves the score much further than shaving actions off level 1.

Overshooting is quadratic, not linear. Twice the baseline actions leaves you at a quarter of the score, not half. Matching the human baseline is 100, and since the per level value is capped at 115, beating the baseline is worth something but not much.

I checked the formula above against the shipped `EnvironmentScoreCalculator` on those three cases and they agree to 1e-9. The reproduction, plus an offline map of all 25 bundled games that runs from the competition wheels with no API key, is here if you want to run it yourself: https://www.kaggle.com/code/busyaprime/arc-agi-3-offline-atlas-and-scoring
